Inclusive confidence makes these inductive checks sufficient. At t≥500 the ramp increment vanishes and for each K the positive gap matrix has row sums 1 and 2/3 in some order, so its square has maximum row sum strictly below one. Therefore a and b converge to 1. For K≥3, the first ordinary gap is at least .305, outside the bound, while the nonnegative source gap is at most .126. A and A′ then keep averaging each other at .07; B follows the source with one-step lag. This is permanent since the ordinary gap stays above .43 and the subsequent source gap is at most .001. This also verifies nonempty eligible neighborhoods in every case. The observable excludes sources and equals (2a+b)/3, so the separated limit is 19/50 and the drop is 31/50. value.rationale: This is a fully solved motivated counterexample to monotone influence in the aggregate input strength at fixed placement. It isolates permanent loss of an otherwise attractive ordinary bridge without repulsion, random source placement, changing ordinary topology, or varying ramp speed. The exact 2-to-3 source cutoff and large limiting loss come from one strict first-step inequality and a proof that the low-strength regimes never rupture; they are not a numerical anomaly. The value is the transparent model witness, not a universal cutoff, minimum number of agents, or behavioral prediction.
